key_insight: DualG-MRAG separates global reasoning from local evidence matching with two graph levels, improving multimodal multi-hop retrieval and generation.
engineering_relevance: The decoupled macro/micro graph design offers a practical way to reduce retrieval noise while preserving fine-grained visual and textual evidence for multimodal QA systems.
method: Builds a Macro Graph for global topological routing across documents and modalities.
Builds a Micro Graph for fine-grained local verification of candidate evidence.
Uses a GNN Retriever with query-driven message passing and dynamic programming decoding to extract reasoning paths for generation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive experiments showing higher evidence recall and better complex QA accuracy than baselines.
watch_item: The dual-graph and dynamic path extraction pipeline may add implementation complexity and runtime overhead, especially for large multimodal corpora.
paper_title: DualG-MRAG: Decoupling Macro-Reasoning and Micro-Matching for Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
